state.case_summary:
A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone) was referred for evaluation of 3 months of hematochezia. He reported two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood; polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding. He denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions. He was intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic. On examination his abdomen was soft and nontender; a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted. Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative. Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa; the rest of the colon appeared normal. Histologic examination of the polyps revealed eroded surface mucosa with reactive hyperplastic glands and marked expansion of the lamina propria by a dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate predominantly composed of pale histiocytes with vacuolated cytoplasm admixed with eosinophils, neutrophils, and lymphocytes. The histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains. Additional fungal (Grocott–Gömöri’s methenamine silver) and acid-fast (Kinyoun) stains were negative for organisms.
